Automated Model Briefing

⚠ AI-generated text — may be wrong, incomplete, or overconfident. This is automated commentary on experimental model output, not flight advice and not a weather forecast. It has not been reviewed by a meteorologist.

Overall Assessment A sharp-lapse-rate day with moderate to strong thermals and variable winds. Ridge soaring is mostly unfavourable due to off-wind directions, but thermal flying is good at Rainbow Ridge and Duck Hill in the afternoon. Advanced skills are essential where lapse rates exceed 8 °C/km.

Site Breakdown

  • Kingsbury grade: Marginal – wind direction off for ridge soaring; thermals flyable but sharp (8.3 °C/km). Window 9am–4pm, peak 385 fpm, ceiling 2867 ft AGL. Advanced pilots only.
  • Hallelujah: Marginal – ridge soaring unfavourable (wind off except 10am); thermal soaring possible with crosswind. Sharp thermals (9.5 °C/km). Window 11am–5pm, peak 460 fpm, ceiling 4959 ft AGL.
  • Slide Mountain: Favorable – light winds aligned with launch, no sharp thermals. Window 10am–4pm, peak 362 fpm, ceiling 1924 ft AGL.
  • McClellan: Marginal – favourable wind direction only until late morning, then cross. Notable low‑level shear (6 mph speed, 36° turn). Sharp thermals (8.9 °C/km). Brief window 10am–12pm, peak 430 fpm, ceiling 3537 ft AGL.
  • West McClellan: Unfavourable for ridge soaring (wind off all day). Thermal flying possible if off‑wind tolerated. Sharp thermals (8.2 °C/km). Window 12:30pm–4pm, peak 426 fpm, ceiling 3750 ft AGL.
  • Peavine Mountain: Marginal – wind direction off after 9am, later crosswind. No sharp thermals. Window 1pm–4pm, peak 387 fpm, ceiling 2676 ft AGL.
  • Rainbow Ridge: Favorable – wind direction mostly aligned, strong thermals but sharp (9.6 °C/km). Advanced pilots only. Window 10am–5pm, peak 494 fpm, ceiling 4908 ft AGL.
  • Duck Hill: Favorable for afternoon thermal/light ridge soaring. Sharp thermals (9.4 °C/km), note low‑level speed shear (6 mph). Window 12pm–6pm, peak 462 fpm, ceiling 4710 ft AGL.
  • Daydreams: Unfavorable – strong off‑wind and weak thermals. No flyable window.

Hazards

  • Sharp thermals (lapse rate >8 °C/km) at Kingsbury, Hallelujah, McClellan, West McClellan, Rainbow Ridge, Duck Hill – advanced/expert pilots only.
  • Low‑level wind shear at McClellan (6 mph speed change, 36° directional change) and Duck Hill (6 mph speed change) – increased turbulence risk.
  • Rotor/lee turbulence downwind of Peavine Mountain and Carson Range ridges possible due to shifting wind directions (westerly early, easterly mid‑morning, variable afternoon).
  • Moderate thermal turbulence in strongest cores (domain‑wide σw 2.1 m/s) – caution in rough air.

Site Forecast ?Top of Thermals (PBLH) — height of the turbulent mixing layer; thermals typically reach this ceiling.
LCL (Lifted Condensation Level) — altitude where rising air reaches its dew point; theoretical cloud base.
Cloud Base — lowest model level with >10% cloud fraction.
w* — convective velocity scale; higher = stronger thermals (ft/min).
Cloud Cover — max cloud fraction over the column (0–100%).
Wind thresholds: orange = 12 mph, red = 18 mph.
